headerDisplay: Homebridge plugin for TP-Link TAPO security cameras.
footerDisplay: If your video feed is not working, try to check if any of the parameters at the video config can be tuned. You can use https://homebridge-plugins.github.io/homebridge-camera-ffmpeg/configs to check if someone has already found the right values for your camera.

name.title: Name
name.description: Set the camera name for display in the Home app

username.title: TAPO username
username.description: Most of the time you should leave this empty, defaulting to admin. If it doesn't work, try to use your streaming username (see below)

password.title: TAPO password
password.description: Password of your TAPO Cloud (the one you use to login the application, not the password for the RTSP configuration). If it doesn't work, try to use your streaming password (see below)

streamUser.title: Stream User
streamUser.description: Username to access the RTSP video feed and ONVIF motion sensor (You can find it in TAPO app > Settings > Advanced Settings > Camera Account). Required unless both streaming and the motion sensor are disabled. Note: This must be only alphanumeric [A-Za-z0-9], no special characters allowed!

streamPassword.title: Stream Password
streamPassword.description: Password to access the RTSP video feed and ONVIF motion sensor (You can find it in TAPO app > Settings > Advanced Settings > Camera Account). Required unless both streaming and the motion sensor are disabled. Note: This must be only alphanumeric [A-Za-z0-9], no special characters allowed!

pullInterval.title: Pull Interval
pullInterval.description: Numbers of milliseconds after we update accessories by polling the status of the camera

debug.title: Debug
debug.description: Enables debugging of the underlying camera-ffmpeg plugin

twoWayAudio.title: Two-Way Audio (Talkback)
twoWayAudio.description: Enables two-way audio (talkback) so you can speak to the camera directly from the Apple Home app live stream without using the Tapo app. Note: Ensure 'Third-Party Compatibility' is enabled in the Tapo app (Me > Tapo Lab > Third-Party Compatibility).

returnAudioTarget.title: Return Audio Target (FFmpeg output)
returnAudioTarget.description: Optional custom FFmpeg output target for routing talkback return audio from the Apple Home app (e.g. to a local go2rtc instance, RTP stream, or audio bridge endpoint). Example: '-acodec pcm_alaw -ar 8000 -ac 1 -f rtp rtp://127.0.0.1:5004'.

debugReturn.title: Debug Two-Way Audio
debugReturn.description: Enables verbose logging for the two-way return audio FFmpeg process in Homebridge logs.

hsv.title: HomeKit Secure Video (HSV)
hsv.description: Enables HomeKit Secure Video for this camera. When enabled, the camera stream is also configured for recording and motion-triggered event clips in Apple Home.

hksvConfig.title: HSV Advanced Options
hksvConfig.description: Optional advanced video and audio encoding configuration for HomeKit Secure Video recordings.

source.title: Custom Recording Source
source.description: Custom stream input for HSV recordings (leave empty to use the default RTSP feed).

vcodec.title: Recording Video Codec
vcodec.description: Video encoder for HSV recordings. Default is 'libx264' (transcoding for full HomeKit compatibility) or 'copy'.

acodec.title: Recording Audio Codec
acodec.description: Audio codec for HSV recording. Default is 'aac'.

audio.title: Record Audio
audio.description: Include audio in HomeKit Secure Video recordings.

maxWidth.title: Recording Max Width
maxWidth.description: Override maximum video width for HSV recordings.

maxHeight.title: Recording Max Height
maxHeight.description: Override maximum video height for HSV recordings.

maxFPS.title: Recording Max FPS
maxFPS.description: Override maximum framerate for HSV recordings.

maxBitrate.title: Recording Max Bitrate
maxBitrate.description: Override maximum bitrate (in kbit/s) for HSV recordings.

encoderOptions.title: Custom Encoder Options
encoderOptions.description: Custom FFmpeg encoding parameters for HSV video.

disableEyesToggleAccessory.title: Disable Eyes toggle
disableEyesToggleAccessory.description: Disables the eyes (privacy mode) switch accessory

disableMotionDetectionToggleAccessory.title: Disable Motion Detection toggle
disableMotionDetectionToggleAccessory.description: Disables the Motion Detection switch accessory

enableFloodLightAccessory.title: Enable Floodlight toggle
enableFloodLightAccessory.description: Enables the Floodlight lightbulb accessory (opt-in because not all cameras support it)

enableNightVisionSensor.title: Enable Darkness / Night Vision Sensor
enableNightVisionSensor.description: Exposes a sensor to Apple Home that detects when the camera is in dark / infrared night vision mode (black & white) versus normal daylight mode. Enables automations such as turning on lights only when motion is detected in the dark.

nightVisionSensorType.title: Darkness Sensor Type
nightVisionSensorType.description: Type of HomeKit sensor to expose. Occupancy Sensor is recommended because it can be used directly as a condition in Apple Home automations ('When Motion Detected, IF Darkness is Occupied -> Turn on Light').

nightVisionSensorName.title: Darkness Sensor Name
nightVisionSensorName.description: Custom display name for the Darkness / Night Vision sensor accessory

nightVisionPollInterval.title: Darkness Check Interval (seconds)
nightVisionPollInterval.description: Frequency in seconds to sample the camera's day/night state in the background (default: 5s). Note: An immediate check is also triggered automatically whenever motion is detected.

nightVisionThreshold.title: Color Saturation Threshold
nightVisionThreshold.description: Sensitivity threshold for black-and-white night vision detection (default: 6.0).

lowQuality.title: Low Quality
lowQuality.description: Video stream will be requested in low-quality instead of high-quality

rtspTransport.title: RTSP Transport
rtspTransport.description: Transport protocol used to receive the camera RTSP stream. TCP is the default for stable video streaming without packet drops or lag; try UDP if preferred on low-latency wired networks.

motionDetectionToggleAccessoryName.title: Motion Detection toggle Name
motionDetectionToggleAccessoryName.description: Name of the Motion Detection toggle

videoMaxWidth.title: Video Max Width
videoMaxWidth.description: The maximum width used for video streamed to HomeKit. If set to 0, or videoCodec is set to 'copy' (default), the resolution of the source is used. If not set, will use any size HomeKit requests.

videoMaxHeight.title: Video Max Height
videoMaxHeight.description: The maximum height used for video streamed to HomeKit. If set to 0, or videoCodec is set to 'copy' (default), the resolution of the source is used. If not set, will use any size HomeKit requests.

videoMaxFPS.title: Video Max FPS
videoMaxFPS.description: The maximum frame rate used for video streamed to HomeKit. If set to 0, or videoCodec is set to 'copy' (default), the framerate of the source is used. If not set, will use any framerate HomeKit requests.

videoMaxBitrate.title: Video Max Bitrate
videoMaxBitrate.description: The maximum bitrate used for video streamed to HomeKit, in kbit/s. If not set, or videoCodec is set to 'copy' (default), it will use any bitrate HomeKit requests.

videoPacketSize.title: Video Packet Size
videoPacketSize.description: If audio or video is choppy try a smaller value. If not set, or videoCodec is set to 'copy' (default), it will use any packet size HomeKit requests.

videoForceMax.title: Force Max Video
videoForceMax.description: If set, the settings requested by HomeKit will be overridden with any 'maximum' values defined in this config. If videoCodec is set to 'copy' (default), this setting set to true is useless.

videoCodec.title: Video Codec
videoCodec.description: Set the codec used for encoding video sent to HomeKit, must be H.264-based. You can change to a hardware accelerated video codec with this option, if one is available. By default, we set 'copy' to avoid any video processing happening on the Homebridge server and disregarding any max values set above, but this also means possibly sending more video data to your devices than necessary, and some Homekit clients may not like not receiving the resolutions/fps they asked for. If you select a custom codec and your ffmpeg process is crashing, it most likely can't handle the video codec you've chosen.
